titlePlain: Writing a Dockerfile That Builds Fast and Stays
subtitle: Lesson 2 · Docker for Platform Engineers

caption: Everything not excluded gets sent to the daemon before a single instruction runs.

steps.label: Dependency manifest
steps.sub: COPY package.json + RUN npm ci — changes occasionally

code:
# Slow: COPY . . before install invalidates npm ci every time
FROM node:20-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN npm ci --omit=dev

# Fast: install layer stays cached across source changes
FROM node:20.17.0-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY . .
caption: A cache miss on any instruction invalidates every layer after it.

eyebrow: Clean up inside the same layer
code:
# Wrong: cleanup in a later RUN can't remove an earlier layer's bytes
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
RUN rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Right: install and cleanup commit as one layer
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
caption: Chaining with && keeps the apt cache out of the committed layer entirely.
